purpose: Separates the four independent claim-side decisions so none silently implies another. NOTHING is activated in this sprint.

claim_review.question: Is this particular claim sufficiently supported by admitted evidence?

claim_approval.question: Has governance approved this exact claim boundary?
claim_approval.note: e.g. CLM-TERM-MOS2-DE-001 is approved at claim level.

claim_registry_operational_activation.question: May APPROVED claims from this registry be consumed by reference surfaces?

route_publication.question: May a particular knowledge surface use them publicly?

independence_invariants: evidence_verified does NOT imply claim_review passed
an approved claim in an inactive registry is NOT consumable
coarseness_finding: Current registries carry a single registry-wide status: inactive|active. This is too coarse: it cannot activate one approved, admitted claim without activating an entire registry of mostly pending claims.

scoped_activation_proposal.status: PROPOSAL ONLY — not applied this sprint; activates nothing
scoped_activation_proposal.mechanism: Replace registry-wide activation with per-claim operational activation gated on: claim_approval == approved AND every supporting evidence record is evidence_verified with a valid source-use qualification AND no prohibited-use conflict. Registry-level 'active' would then mean 'this registry MAY contain individually-activatable claims', not 'all its claims are live'.
scoped_activation_proposal.regression: If any supporting evidence or qualification regresses, the claim's operational activation regresses to inactive (never raises).

this_sprint: No registry activated. No claim approved or changed. No activation records created. CLM-TERM-MOS2-DE-001 remains approved-but-not-activated (terminology_claims.json status: inactive).
